answer: Surveyed ground = (elev_ft - height_above_gnd) ft x 0.3048 (NAVD88 m), compared to the 3DEP bare-earth DEM (m, NAVD88) sampled at each mark. 152 of 159 marks were usable (7 have no height_above_gnd). For the 121 exterior marks, DEM minus survey has bias -0.01 m, median -0.02 m, RMSE 0.32 m, MAE 0.19 m, 90th percentile 0.50 m; 57% of all 152 marks are within 0.15 m, 84% within 0.5 m. Including 31 marks flagged interior/garage-type (survey ground there is often a floor, not terrain), bias is +0.17 m and RMSE 0.77 m, with outliers up to 5.3 m. The DEM is unbiased on average at street-level marks, with roughly 0.3 m random error, which is the same size as typical shallow flood depths.
traps_or_caveats: CSV line 1 is a citation; header is line 2 (parsed accordingly).
Units: elev_ft and height_above_gnd are feet, DEM is meters; converted ft->m (x0.3048). Both NAVD88, so no datum shift applied.
7 marks (e.g. 41625, 41100) have empty height_above_gnd so surveyed ground is undefined; excluded, not filled.

Interior flag is a keyword regex (basement, garage, inside, apartment...) on description/notes; it is loose (flags 'garage door' exterior walls and a 'playground wheel'). Interior-type marks measure height from a floor, which inflates DEM-minus-survey (up to +5.3 m at two Queens marks 40980/41629 with 0.9 m local DEM relief, likely slope/building-edge); report exterior stats as the headline.

Survey ground is the ground at the mark's base (hand-measured height), while the DEM is a ~2 m cell: horizontal error from phone/car GPS positions (all 159 marks) and local slope (median 3x3 DEM range 0.25 m, up to 3 m) add scatter; nearest-cell sampling used, 3x3 min/mean/max give similar or worse fits.

DEM is bare-earth 3DEP lidar-derived, not dated to Sept 2021; construction or regrading since collection is not captured. Marks on walls/lamp posts near steep park edges (e.g. 41610, 41307 Prospect Park) show about -1 m error.
Height-above-gnd values of exactly 0.0 (11 marks) may be placeholders; kept as given.
Duplicate coordinates exist (multiple marks at the same site, e.g. 41146/41587), so errors are not fully independent.
Tiles are Web Mercator (EPSG:3857, ~2.63 m cell in map units, ~2 m on the ground at this latitude).
